D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official list contains five read-oriented query tools; no write or destructive operation is listed. Tool annotations such as readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, and openWorldHint are not published. 2. No server-enforced confirmation, preview-confirm flow, elicitation, or approval workflow for these tools was documented. 3. OAuth is required. Metadata exposes scopes mcp, claudeai, openid, profile, email, mdcapp, tenants, groups. Moody’s says users need authorized credentials; inheritance of product roles, admin switches, client allowlists, redirect URI review, token duration, and revocation behavior are not described. 4. Streamable HTTP and one global endpoint are documented. No read-only mode, toolset filter, query-free mode, sandbox, or regional endpoint for this input server was found. 5. The product terms for covered solutions delivered by MCP/Smart API restrict AI use to specified internal purposes, require a private AI-tool instance, and prohibit training language models on covered solutions/product output. These terms’ applicability depends on the customer’s agreement and order form. No tool-level field masking or PII filtering is documented. 6. No endpoint rate limits, quotas, bulk caps, time limits, truncation, or per-call costs were found. 7. Tool parameter schemas and validation behavior are not published. 8. Moody’s blog claims, generally, that interactions are authenticated and logged and that requests and responses are logged in full; endpoint-specific audit fields, retention, and opt-out are not specified. 9. No feedback, rating, report, survey, or upsell tools or instructions appear in the reviewed official list. 10. No server-delivered skills or behavioral instructions were found; official tool descriptions state functions. 11. No persistent agent memory or history-dependent tool behavior was documented. 12. The input is presented as a hosted remote endpoint. Moody’s separately announced a purpose-built MCP application for Agentic Solutions in Claude; its relationship to this endpoint is not established. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or comparable escape-hatch tool appears in the official list.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The documented input endpoint presents one flat tool list. The separate Claude MCP application announcement does not establish a nested structure for this endpoint.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool reference exists at https://www.moodys.com/web/en/us/genai/model-context-protocol.html and names 5 tools. It states no numeric total. The Claude connector directory lists 15 names; Skills Playground also reports 15; Tool Junction reports 16 entries, including one blank tool entry; RevampKey reports 15. The Claude directory’s 15 names overlap with four official names, so 11 catalogue-only names were added. The official getEntityRatingDrivers name is not in the 15-name catalogue list. Tool Junction and Skills Playground corroborate the endpoint URL. Claude connector directory is a third-party listing, regardless of its directory status. Actions contain the 5 official names plus 11 catalogue-only names.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The official setup guide tells users to “verify if all tools are available and enabled” after connecting. This is client-side guidance; no server enforcement is described.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Moody’s blog states: “Every request and response is logged in full, creating a transparent chain of custody that supports internal audit and regulatory review.” Its product terms state that when covered solutions are delivered via MCP/Smart API, use is subject to restrictions including internal use and a prohibition on using covered solutions or product output to train a language model.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The official page says the OAuth flow “ensures secure access” to Moody’s proprietary data. Moody’s blog describes the access as authenticated, logged, and compliant with enterprise data policies.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth is corroborated by endpoint metadata and the 401 response. Logging, full request/response capture, and policy compliance are general Moody’s documentation claims; their implementation details are not exposed in endpoint documentation. Contractual AI-use restrictions are documented, but no tool-level enforcement mechanism is described. The secure-access assurance is not elaborated beyond OAuth.

contradictions: The official tool reference names five tools, including getEntityRatingDrivers. Claude’s third-party connector listing reports 15 names but omits getEntityRatingDrivers and instead includes getEntityCreditUpgradeDowngradeFactors. Their equivalence is not established by the reviewed sources.

The Claude directory and Skills Playground report 15 tools; Tool Junction reports 16 entries, one of which is blank. After retaining the official five and adding catalogue-only names, the combined list has 16 distinct names.

OAuth scope metadata includes mcp, claudeai, openid, profile, email, mdcapp, tenants, and groups, but the official tool list does not map scopes to individual tools or describe these scopes’ permissions.
observations_for_research: The endpoint requires OAuth, and the authorization metadata exposes both user-oriented and service-oriented grant types, including authorization code, refresh token, client credentials, and token exchange.
The public official reference provides functional descriptions for five tools but no input schemas, annotations, complete tool-result examples, or initialize instructions.
Third-party tool inventories give a wider 15-name list, but their naming differs from the official rating-driver tool and they do not publish parameter schemas in the reviewed sources.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, pages/INDEX.txt, relevant official page text and HTML/script extracts, and the local code folder. No official repository or package was listed or present in code/. The endpoint and install path returned HTTP 401; the supplied OAuth metadata was used without re-fetching. The official tool-reference page and its available page material were checked for tool names. Third-party sources used to supplement the official five-tool list: Claude connector directory, Skills Playground, Tool Junction, and RevampKey. The unrelated community Moody’s repositories were not used as evidence. The separate RMS Platform endpoint was not established as this server or as a Moody’s corporate endpoint.
